# Independent audit: free-mass raw-moment selector and quantile lift

Both audited notes pass, with their stated limited scopes.

## Free-mass raw moment width selector

Source: `candidate e16770c76630ebf6`.
I also read and ran `supporting computation verify_free_mass_raw_moment_width_obstruction.py`;
its exact Fraction checks pass.

The four widths `(2,16,17,1)` have decreasing successive differences,
so the hypograph of their piecewise affine interpolation, together with
the upper boundary zero, gives a full-dimensional convex body with
exactly the four stated positive integer fibers. The total mass is 36,
and bases 1 and 2 are exactly its marginal median bases.

The endpoint rearrangement formulas cover every dominated measurable
source: for a fixed mass in an interval, an upper interval maximizes
its first moment and a lower interval minimizes it. Allowing different
mass vectors for the two moment endpoints, with a common total mass
and the same prescribed base mean, therefore gives exactly the stated
joint quadratic program. Its Hessian is minus the identity on both
mass vectors, so the displayed feasible KKT certificates prove unique
global optima, not merely stationary candidates.

At base 1, the equality multipliers give residuals
`(23/2,0,0,-15/4)` and `(0,0,0,-87/4)`; their signs agree with the
appropriate active box constraints. The moments are
`A=-1089/32`, `B=4101/32`, yielding raw width `753/8` and normalized
midpoint `-2595/376`. At base 2, the analogous residuals are
`(-6,0,0,14)` and `(-21,0,0,0)`, giving width `351/4` and midpoint
`-123/16`. At the endpoint bases, balance forces sources into their
own fibers and direct one-variable maximization gives widths 1 and
one quarter. These exhaust every feasible integer base.

Thus the unique joint maximum is at the median base 1. The displayed
closed caps have exact masses `3347/376` and `139/16`, with respective
deficits `37/376` and `5/16` below `M/4=9`. Large outward base tilts
isolate a half interval at each endpoint, so those other two candidates
also fail. All selected points lie in their actual fibers. This
disproves both the best-among-all-base optima and the joint optimum
rules, including restriction to marginal median bases. It makes no
claim about the deepest point of the body or about other points in
the source moment intervals.

## Concave volume-quantile lift

Source: `candidate b84198b3fe4ca80c`.

The nonempty-cap clause is precisely what makes the hypograph argument
valid at `t=0`. It retains every lower-dimensional real-base fiber and
assigns it the actual maximum of the affine functional. Brunn--Minkowski
applies to averages with nonempty zero-volume caps as well as to two
positive-volume caps. Compactness of the original body ensures that
nonempty limiting caps stay nonempty; containment in shrinking compact
neighborhoods gives the required upper semicontinuity of cap volumes.
Consequently the stated joint domain is convex and the inverse is a
finite upper semicontinuous concave function, including all its zero
root boundary points.

For positive-volume fibers, the one-dimensional projection of their
uniform measure has no atoms and has strictly increasing distribution
between its extreme values. The survival quantile transformation and
the substitution of `t^d` therefore give the exact first-moment
formula, with its factor `d t^(d-1)`. Zero-volume fibers contribute
zero to all the mixed-volume sums; they are retained geometrically in
the lift and are not assigned a false positive measure. The cap-root
formula concerns closed caps, whose nonvertical boundaries have zero
fiber volume. On a zero-volume fiber the descriptions 'zero cap
volume' and 'full cap volume' coincide, without affecting that formula.

The true-centroid equations and the stationary tilt equations use
different weights and are not conflated. Under the explicitly stated
regularity and absence of endpoint contacts, implicit differentiation
has positive sign
`partial_v c_z=(z-j)/beta_z`, and coarea identifies
`d c_z^(d-1)/beta_z` with section measure divided by `||u||`. Only proper
positive-volume fibers contribute to that derivative. Whole or empty
fibers have locally constant cap mass under these hypotheses.

In dimension one, interpreting normalization to continuous coefficient
one as a positive rescaling after choosing the orientation of the
continuous coordinate gives `U=upper-t` and section weight one. A
coordinate reflection, if needed, preserves the mixed lattice and
does not reverse the chosen cap. No extension of the differential
identities to nonsmooth endpoint contacts is asserted. The result is
an exact lift and two centering laws, not a depth lower bound.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
